freshly_checked_applications.status: primary statement, scope and arithmetic Frobenius convention checked
freshly_checked_applications.reference: J. S. Milne, Algebraic Number Theory, version 3.08 (19 July 2020), Theorem 8.31, printed p.147; arithmetic Frobenius convention preceding 8.14, printed p.141
freshly_checked_applications.statement_used: Every conjugacy class in a finite Galois extension of number fields occurs as the unramified arithmetic Frobenius class at a positive density of base primes.
hypotheses_checked: Choose open normal U0 inside the original open U; its fixed field F/E is finite Galois.
Take Eprime/Q finite Galois inside the same Omega, containing F and E; the actual prescribed g restricts to h in Gal(Eprime/E).
Apply the theorem over the number field Q to the conjugacy class of h; all ramified primes and the rational primes below the finite forbidden set are excluded.
Conjugation of the chosen prime makes its Frobenius exactly h. No effectiveness, GRH, class field theory or asymptotic prime bound is used.
derived_matching: CAP6 proves degree-one absolute norm because h fixes E, so every residue element satisfies x^p=x.
CAP6 writes the elementary finite valuation/transitivity/Frobenius and compact inverse-limit matching into the original algebraic closure.
CAP7 proves actual CM splitting and realizes an arbitrary finite list with injective base primes.
CAP11 selects the inverse target coset and explicitly proves the inverse-Frobenius approximation and tame sign.

note: The new external application is unconditional finite-Galois Chebotarev, with actual field extension, excluded primes and arithmetic Frobenius convention checked. The remaining new arguments are written independently. Earlier checked published inputs retain their original scopes; CohP is retained, not silently replaced by a new literature claim.
